trust_decision.summary: Whether a user-supplied URL (or redirect Location) may be fetched server-side is decided by matching its literal/resolved IP against the BLOCKED_RANGES deny-list in _is_ip_blocked, called from _is_safe_canonical_url.

landing_point.why: The summary names is_safe_url() in html_to_markdown and 'incomplete IP range blocking'; the deny-list constant is the obvious first stop.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST /query with module=html_to_markdown and a 'url' key (misp_modules/__main__.py:324, misp_modules/__main__.py:232 -> html_to_markdown.py:127-129 -> fetchHTML), plus the public helper is_safe_url (html_to_markdown.py:83)
fix_sites.module_kind: expansion module (deny-list constant used by the shared URL check)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: misp_modules/modules/expansion/qrcode.py:57-76 (own is_safe_url using is_loopback/is_private/is_reserved; no shared-address-space 100.64.0.0/10 or multicast coverage), used by fetch_url_image at misp_modules/modules/expansion/qrcode.py:84

O3_reason_to_dismiss: qrcode is a different module with its own SSRF guard built on Python's is_private/is_reserved, so a solver can argue the advisory names only html_to_markdown's hand-written BLOCKED_RANGES and qrcode already 'uses the stdlib properly'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Public documentation-range addresses must stay fetchable: tests require 192.0.2.1 and ::ffff:192.0.2.1 (and a hostname resolving to 192.0.2.1) to pass is_safe_url, and a safe redirect to 192.0.2.2 to be followed; the tempting `not ip.is_global` / `ip.is_private` rewrite rejects 192.0.2.0/24 and breaks these. The raw_html path must also keep working without any fetch.

O6_input_shapes: IPv6 literal host in brackets (::, fc00::/7, fe80::/10) — fix.diff:20,22-23
IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal (::ffff:0.0.0.0, ::ffff:100.64.0.1), via existing _normalize_ip_address at misp_modules/modules/expansion/html_to_markdown.py:41-43 — fix.diff:43-44
hostname resolving via getaddrinfo to a blocked address (ULA) — misp_modules/modules/expansion/html_to_markdown.py:51-54, fix.diff:51-56
redirect Location re-checked through the same list — misp_modules/modules/expansion/html_to_markdown.py:99-102

O8_uncovered_routes.route: qrcode URL fetch: own SSRF guard misses shared address space 100.64.0.0/10 (and multicast), the same range class this fix adds
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different module and different guard implementation (stdlib predicates, not BLOCKED_RANGES); report only names html_to_markdown.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: qrcode URL fetch follows redirects without re-checking the target address (requests.get default allow_redirects)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Redirect handling is a different mechanism from the range list and the module already advertises 'SSRF Protection'.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: html_to_markdown after the fix still lets IPv4-compatible IPv6 (::a.b.c.d, e.g. ::7f00:1), 6to4/NAT64 embeddings, multicast 224.0.0.0/4 and 240.0.0.0/4 through, because only ipv4_mapped is unwrapped
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Exotic/deprecated IPv6 forms and non-unicast ranges look out of the advisory's 'private ranges' list; reachability depends on host routing.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Normalisation unwraps only ipv4_mapped; a sibling unwrap gap for sixtofour/ipv4-compatible forms is a how-type canonicalisation sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainer already added one IPv6 unwrap for mapped addresses and plausibly stopped there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second, independently written SSRF guard at distance that a fix to BLOCKED_RANGES never touches.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already exists at the pinned commit; written by a different author with stdlib predicates.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared lib helper doing urlopen could realistically host a planted 'fetch arbitrary URL' helper reusing html_to_markdown's check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: misp_modules/lib holds cross-module HTTP helpers; a maintainer factoring out a fetch helper would put it there.

O9_family: SSRF: incomplete IP deny-list / address canonicalisation (CWE-918, CWE-20)

O10_build.toolchain: Python >=3.10 (pyproject.toml:18), pip/poetry; deps include requests, markdownify (pyproject.toml:28), bs4; qrcode needs opencv-python (pyproject.toml:106) and pyzbar/libzbar (pyproject.toml:125)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_html_to_markdown.py (unittest, getaddrinfo and requests.Session mocked, offline); tests/test_expansions.py:512 covers qrcode attachment path only and needs a running server

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Append the four missing CIDRs to BLOCKED_RANGES (or swap to `not ip.is_global`, which blocks 192.0.2.0/24 and breaks the allow tests) and never look at qrcode.py's own guard.

out_of_scope_notes: DNS-rebinding TOCTOU: html_to_markdown resolves for the check (html_to_markdown.py:53) and requests resolves again at fetch (html_to_markdown.py:95); different mechanism, not pursued.
onyphe_full.is_routable (misp_modules/modules/expansion/onyphe_full.py:64-85) is an indicator noise filter, not an SSRF guard.
unverified: Repo size in MB not measured.

qrcode gap for 100.64.0.0/10 relies on Python ipaddress semantics (is_private and is_reserved False for shared address space); is_private lists changed across 3.11/3.12 patch releases, so exact coverage depends on interpreter version.
Only expansion modules were grepped for direct user-URL fetches; other modules taking a 'url' attribute that call third-party APIs were judged not to fetch the user URL, without reading each fully.
Whether qrcode's redirect gap counts within this advisory's protection (range blocking) versus a separate mechanism is a judgement call.
Latest-release presence of O8 routes unknown (no latest code provided).
